how_to_read_this: Every external thing ARGUS needs is listed here ONCE, with the four facts that decide
whether it may be acquired: where it comes from, which revision, how its bytes are
verified, and what its licence permits.
UNKNOWN IS A LITERAL VALUE, NEVER A BLANK. A field reading UNKNOWN carries a
why_unknown beside it and makes the component unverifiable, which is a REFUSAL in
`argus setup` rather than a warning. No hash and no licence in this file was invented;
an invented one is indistinguishable from a measured one once it is written down, and
that is the whole reason the field exists.
NO ABSOLUTE PATH APPEARS HERE. Where a component lands is decided by the path contract
(argus.core.paths) at run time. A machine-specific path baked into shipped config is a
file a stranger cannot use and cannot even diagnose.

integrity_modes.SHA256: one immutable file; the digest below is checked after transfer and a mismatch is a refusal
integrity_modes.GIT_REVISION: a repository pinned at a full 40-character commit; the commit IS the content address
integrity_modes.GIT_REVISION_ABBREVIATED: a pin recorded only in short form. NOT accepted as verification: a short prefix is not the address, and resolving it needs the very repository whose contents are in question
integrity_modes.PER_OBJECT_MANIFEST: a live prefix of many objects with no single digest. Integrity is per object, recorded in ACQUIRE_MANIFEST.json at fetch time by argus.core.acquisition_identity. Declared, not invented
integrity_modes.UNKNOWN: no content address is known to this project. Acquisition refuses

components.name: ScrollPrize villa (volume-cartographer, vc_render_tifxyz)
components.purpose: the official CT-to-surface sampler and segmentation tooling. ARGUS shells out to it and never links it in
components.version: pinned commit; see argus/upstream.lock.json for the same pin and its clone flags

licence.permits: run as an external subprocess. NOT incorporated into ARGUS, and if a build of it is ever distributed the source-offer obligation attaches

components.why_unknown: a blob:none depth-1 clone's size depends on what git decides to fetch; argus/upstream.lock.json records 268435456 bytes of .git plus 5003 checked-out files for one observed clone, which is a measurement of that clone and not a promise about yours

components.name: Herculaneum CT volumes (open-data S3)
components.purpose: the scans themselves. Fetched per region of interest, never bundled

integrity.why_unknown: a prefix of millions of chunk objects has no single digest. Each object is hashed as it lands and recorded in the store's ACQUIRE_MANIFEST.json, which is what a resume and a seal are checked against

licence.permits: fetch and use. NOT redistribution -- the installer must not bundle a byte of it

components.why_unknown: unbounded: the size acquired is whatever region of interest a run declares, not a property of the component

components.name: ink_9um human ink labels

integrity.why_unknown: the bucket is public but unversioned and this project has pinned no digest for it. Publicly fetchable is not the same as pinned, and the two are constantly confused

licence.permits: treated as non-redistributable. The dataset declares no licence and the underlying CT is CC BY-NC 4.0

components.why_unknown: the 32 MiB figure is the size measured by argus.core.label_sources for the label set, not a size published by the bucket

components.name: numpy / zarr / fsspec / s3fs

integrity.why_unknown: a wheel digest is per version AND per platform tag, so one hash in this file would be wrong for most machines. The correct pin is a hash-locked requirements file, which this project has not generated: `uv pip compile --generate-hashes`. Until it exists, `argus setup` refuses to fetch these itself and prints the install line for the operator to run under their own package manager, which does verify

components.why_unknown: depends on the resolved dependency set for the host platform
